nodes.body: We do not ship a daemon, a file watcher, or any other resident process that keeps running once the user has closed the TUI. This was settled after the watchdog-2 spike: the resident watcher we prototyped sat at 8-12% CPU while completely idle and kept a laptop's fans audible, which is unacceptable for a tool people leave installed and forget about. Drift and status checks therefore run on demand -- when the user opens a screen or explicitly refreshes -- never on a timer and never from a background thread that outlives the foreground session. Reviving continuous detection would need a new decision, not just an implementation.
nodes.title: DotState runs no resident process
